doc.title: Richard Wyands interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

title: Rhythm and blues, Mel Torme and Cab Calloway
summary: He played for R&B bird groups, and with Mel Torme and Cab Calloway in San Francisco.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: 1959, late 50s, early 60s, rock & roll was starting to obviously be on the scene. Were you required to play some of that kind of music on club dates and so forth?
Yeah? What kind of things would you play?
Rhythm & blues. I played for some of these, we called them bird groups.
Because they had names like The Orioles and the this and the that. That’s why we called them bird groups. But they had rhythm & blues. I played for some of them in San Francisco even.
I know Jerome said he had done some — he sometimes sang and did some of that kind of thing too.

[scats] gink-gink-gink-gink-gink-gink—.. But it wasn’t going to last forever so you made those too. I remember in San Francisco I worked with Mel Torme, he came in so we got a band together to play for him. Of course he played piano also and drums. That was interesting. He wrote all of his own arrangements. Some of them were a little difficult. They were in difficult keys. You would think — being the good range he had, pretty good — it didn’t matter a half step this way or a half step that way. But he wrote them, oh boy, but it was okay. The band was good.
You got familiar with the black notes again.
Oh yeah. The band was good. They could read anything so. Cab Calloway, I worked with him in San Francisco.
